recent_posts.title: How To Get The Current Entity State From Events
recent_posts.summary: Event Sourcing stores application state in events, which are appended to a log as the source of truth. The process involves building the current entity state from events by retrieving, sorting, and applying them sequentially. Snapshots provide a technical optimization but are not always necessary, as downloading multiple small events poses minimal overhead. Stream aggregation, a pattern in Event Sourcing, allows for efficient debugging and testing by keeping event history accessible.

recent_posts.title: What is Event Sourcing?
recent_posts.summary: Event sourcing is a data persistence technique where each change in an entity's state is stored as a separate event. This approach contrasts with traditional state-oriented persistence that only records the current state. By using domain events, each state mutation is explicitly captured, enabling more transparent and thorough tracking of changes. Applying this method involves altering existing application code to produce and handle these events effectively, offering benefits like better historical tracking and clearer depiction of domain activities.

recent_posts.title: Archiving: Keep your data hot and cold
recent_posts.summary: KurrentDB v25.0 introduces the Archiving feature, allowing users to move older data to external storage like S3. This practice reduces primary disk space usage and optimizes cost by keeping frequently accessed data (hot) on local disks while storing less accessed data (cold) on cheaper, slower storage. The Archiving feature improves scalability by eliminating volume size limits and simplifies configuration with user-defined retention policies. The implementation involves an Archiver node to manage data uploads to the archive. Detailed configurations and S3 authentication methods are covered.

recent_posts.title: LangGraph Checkpointer on KurrentDB
recent_posts.summary: KurrentDB optimizes workflows by storing state transitions as events, ensuring comprehensive historical records, unlike traditional CRUD systems. This makes it an excellent choice for serving as a checkpointer in LangGraph, an orchestration framework for agentic systems. KurrentDB's capabilities enhance observability and offer features like trace export to platforms supporting OTEL. The post includes an example Python Notebook demonstrating integration.

recent_posts.title: 10 problems event sourcing solves
recent_posts.summary: Event Sourcing can address numerous functional and technical problems in software architectures, from auditing and replaying production issues to supporting offline editing in PWAs and scaling out the read side using CQRS. Although not suitable for every situation, Event Sourcing offers unique advantages, such as enhanced temporal analysis, data replication, and cross-domain communication, making it a valuable choice for complex domains requiring detailed event tracking and flexible rule application.

top_posts.title: Benefits Of Event Sourcing
top_posts.summary: Event Sourcing combined with an event-native database benefits businesses by capturing comprehensive data that traditional methods miss. It improves real-time analytics, machine learning capabilities, competitive advantage, system agility, scalability, and resilience. top_posts.title: Service Oriented Architecture vs Event Driven Architecture
top_posts.summary: What is the difference between event-driven and service-oriented architecture (SOA)? Event-driven architecture sees everything that happens in your system as events. EDA prioritizes and provides the context of a system's messages. SOA is not a style of architecture that allows for sustainable growth, as it introduces complexity.
